not_covered: DeepSeek’s release of DeepSeek-R1 on January 20, 2025 [Source: ev-1] triggered the largest single-day loss in Nvidia's history because it demonstrated that a frontier-class reasoning model could be trained for a fraction of incumbent costs, challenging the thesis that AI capital expenditure and Nvidia demand are protected by compute scale [Source: ev-1].

This revelation showed that US export controls restricting access to H800 chips had forced Chinese labs toward efficiency, meaning scarcity rather than preference drove these economic outcomes [Source: ev-1].

The economics revealed included specific training metrics from DeepSeek’s predecessor, DeepSeek-V3 (released December 26, 2024), which reported using roughly 2.79 million GPU-hours at a claimed cost of about $5.6 million on those restricted H800 chips [Source: ev-1].

Following the R1 release, Nvidia lost approximately $589 billion in market capitalization on January 27, 2025, with about $1 trillion erased across the tech complex as markets repriced this new understanding of AI training costs [Source: ev-1].
